site_name: Amazon Web Services, Bethlehem Road campus, 8180 Bethlehem Road, Manassas, VA

site_name: Amazon Web Services, John Marshall Highway campus (Haymarket), 15395 John Marshall Hwy, Haymarket, VA 20169

lead.notes: This is very likely the contested Haymarket AWS site served by Dominion's Haymarket 230 kV line. A page dated 2019-10-09 that I opened says the line 'is necessary to help power a data centre in Haymarket owned by an Amazon subsidiary', which is forward-looking only. site_name: CloudHQ, Manassas (probably the MDC campus), 10400 Harry J Parrish Blvd, Manassas, VA 20110

lead.notes: CloudHQ's own pages give coordinates of 38.73088,-77.50829 for the MDC campus, about 350 m from this permit's point, and 38.71955,-77.49819 for the MCC campus, about 1.2 km away. Directory listings put MDC-1 at 10430 Harry J Parrish Blvd. The MDC page (2023 footer) still says MDC1 'can be ready for service in less than twenty-two months from commitment', so it gives no opening. Data Center Frontier (2017-08-08) reports that CloudHQ completed MCC1 at the Manassas Corporate Center, but I cannot tie MCC1 to 10400 Harry J Parrish, so I did not use 2017. The permit company, Cashvad Ventures LLC, turned up nothing.

site_name: CyrusOne NVA9 (Sterling IX), 43290 Old Ox Road, Sterling, VA 20166

lead.notes: CyrusOne's own NVA9 fact sheet ('Sterling IX location map', PDF created 2020-06-18, hosted on datacentermap's static server) gives the address as 43290 Old Ox Road, which ties NVA9 to this site. site_name: CyrusOne NVA5-NVA7 campus (Sterling V), 21350 Pacific Blvd, Sterling, VA 20166
year_evidence_quote: In mid-2017 the company opened its Sterling V facility, its largest project yet.
year_site_match: The same article describes Sterling V as "a 1 million square foot data center campus on Pacific Boulevard in Sterling." CyrusOne's own NVA5 fact sheet (PDF, rendered and read) gives the address 21350 Pacific Blvd., Sterling, VA 20166 and "approximately 1 million data center square feet at full build"; the fetch tool reported the PDF's metadata title refers to a "Sterling V" location map (metadata reported by the tool, not seen by me in the rendered pages). Sterling V = NVA5 on Pacific Blvd.
verification: Data Center Frontier (Rich Miller, 2018-07-26) states outright, in retrospect, that Sterling V opened in mid-2017. This is a trade-press statement one year after the fact, not a contemporaneous opening release. The CyrusOne NVA5-NVA7 web page opened but carries no address or dates. The fact sheet is a CyrusOne-branded document hosted on a directory site's file server; I used it only to tie the Sterling V name to the 21350 Pacific Blvd address, not as date evidence. The year applies to the first building (NVA5); nothing opened dates NVA6 or NVA7.

site_name: Microsoft Blue Ridge campus (IAD11-12-13), 24282 Quail Ridge Ln, Aldie, VA 20105
year_evidence_quote: Neither data center is operating yet, but their presence is inescapable.
year_site_match: The preceding sentence places the building: "The view from the community landing on Quail Ridge Lake now features the Amazon complex on one side and a 1.5-million-square-foot data center built by Microsoft on the other"; the community is Loudoun Meadows "near Aldie in southeastern Loudoun County." Quail Ridge Lake / Aldie / Microsoft matches 24282 Quail Ridge Ln, Aldie. The page does not give a street address or the IAD11-12-13 name, so the tie is by lake name, town, and operator.
verification: Status is as of 2025-12-01 and is now about eleven months old; it may have changed. The page is a post by an advocacy group (Virginians for a Smarter Digital Future) with a READ MORE link to richmond.com; I infer it is a repost of a Richmond Times-Dispatch article, but richmond.com could not be fetched, so the original and its exact date are unverified. Basis field: no enum value fits a status statement; 'local_news_opening' is used only to label the source type (regional news via advocacy repost), not an opening. The Fox News piece (2026-09-30) is about Statesboro Place in Loudoun County, quotes an anonymous resident that "Only two data centers are active right now," names AWS and Microsoft as operators behind that neighborhood, but does not say which buildings are active and does not mention Quail Ridge, Loudoun Meadows, or Aldie; I could not tie it to this address, so it neither confirms nor overturns the status. No start year is supported.

lead.notes: Smarter Digital Virginia (2025-12-01) describes the Loudoun Meadows community near Aldie, across Quail Ridge Lake from 'a 1.5-million-square-foot data center built by Microsoft', and says 'Neither data center is operating yet.' The Quail Ridge name ties the article to this address. The status is as of December 2025 and may have changed. A Fox News piece (2026-09-30) quotes an anonymous resident saying two nearby data centers are active, but it does not name the operator or the site, so I did not use it. Search results mention a DEQ air permit dated July 2025.

site_name: Microsoft AVC17 (Lakeside), 39 Commerce Drive, Lakeside Commerce Park, east of Clarksville (Boydton mailing address), VA 23917
verification: Two opened pages conflict and neither meets the bar. SoVaNOW (2026-11-04) says "Microsoft is building a data center near Clarksville, and the town is its water utility" and refers to "the Microsoft data center being built nearby," but it never says the site is not operating; a multi-building campus can be under construction with a first building live, and the photo caption reads "Microsoft's data center at the Lakeside Commerce Park in Clarksville." So it does not state not-yet-operating outright. mlq.ai (2026-06-04) says "The AVC17 campus became operational in 2026" and calls it "Microsoft's operational AVC17 campus," but its listed source for AVC17 is Baxtel, a directory, so that is not acceptable evidence for a 2026 start year. It also reports a Virginia DEQ air permit (No. 53086) issued April 2025, which is a permit, not a start. The DCD article was not opened (researcher reported 403; no URL in the record). Left unverified in both directions.

lead.notes: In search results, DCD reports that Microsoft filed for 'AVC17 Lakeside' at Lakeside Commerce Park on Commerce Drive, about 10 miles west of the original Boydton campus. That article returned 403. SoVaNOW (2026-11-04) says 'Microsoft is building a data center near Clarksville' at Lakeside Commerce Park, on U.S. 58 east of Clarksville, which matches this site's coordinates. That page conflicts with mlq.ai (2026-06-04), which says, citing Baxtel, that AVC17 'became operational in 2026'. The datacenter.fyi 'operational Apr 2025' date is only the DEQ permit date. Treat this status as uncertain.
